_note: STARTING POINT — curated by ClauseWise maintainers. Review and extend before each release. Not legal advice; used only for severity comparison within the tool.

typical_patterns.typical: 1–3 months by either party depending on seniority. Should be mutual (same for employer and employee).
red_flags: employee notice longer than employer notice
notice exceeds 6 months
employer can waive notice and pay in lieu but employee cannot
no notice provision at all

typical_patterns.typical: Reasonable geographic and time scope (e.g., 6–12 months, same industry, roles actually competed against). Courts often void overly broad clauses.
red_flags: duration exceeds 2 years
worldwide or unlimited geography
covers any industry not just direct competitors
employee cannot earn a living in their field

typical_patterns.typical: Work created in scope of employment and using company resources belongs to employer. Personal projects on personal time with no company resources excluded.
red_flags: assigns all inventions regardless of use of company resources
covers inventions conceived before employment
no carve-out for personal time/personal projects
moral rights waived without limit

typical_patterns.typical: Cause termination defined clearly (e.g., gross misconduct, repeated policy breach). Without-cause termination on notice or pay-in-lieu.
red_flags: employer sole judge of what constitutes cause
no definition of cause
cause termination with no appeal or cure period
employee terminated for any business reason with no compensation

typical_patterns.typical: 3–6 months with reduced notice (e.g., 1 week). Confirmation of passing probation should be explicit.
red_flags: probation period exceeds 12 months
probation automatically extended indefinitely
no confirmation mechanism
reduced rights not restored after confirmation

typical_patterns.typical: Base salary stated clearly. Bonus criteria objective or at least described. Deductions itemised and legal.
red_flags: bonus entirely discretionary with no criteria
salary can be reduced unilaterally
unpaid overtime implied by 'as needed' language
deductions not specified

typical_patterns.typical: Covers confidential information actually shared in employment. Survives termination for a reasonable period (1–3 years).
red_flags: perpetual confidentiality with no time limit
covers all information employee ever encounters
no carve-out for information already in public domain

typical_patterns.typical: Internal grievance process followed by mediation or employment tribunal. Employee can seek legal advice before agreeing to any settlement.
red_flags: binding arbitration only, no tribunal access
employee must pay employer costs if they lose
mandatory pre-dispute waiver of rights
